rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: Provide funding assistance for sidewalk repairs caused by street tree root damage. Many homeowners and small businesses cannot afford the high cost of repairing sidewalks uplifted or cracked by tree roots, even though the trees are City property, and cant afford to wait for a reimbursement months/years.
rows.headline: Other capital budget request for DPR
rows.response: Agency supports and can accommodate Explanation: NYC Parks' Trees & Sidewalks Program can help repair severe sidewalk damage caused by tree root growth in front of one-, two-, or three-family properties that are owner-occupied and used exclusively for residential purposes (NYC Tax Class 1). Funding for this program is limited, and repairs are made based on a rating system that includes the severity of damage, amount of pedestrian traffic, and the size and condition of the tree. If you are a homeowner with time-sensitive needs for sidewalk repair, or you own a non-Tax Class 1 property that is not eligible for Parks’ Trees & Sidewalks Program, repairing the sidewalk through an independent contractor is often the quickest solution. Anyone performing work on or within 50 feet of a City tree must obtain a Tree Work Permit from Parks before beginning work. If you wish to file a claim against the City of New York for the cost of repairs you performed to your sidewalk because of damage that you believe was caused by a City tree, you may do so by filing a claim with the New York City Comptroller’s Office within 90 days of performing the repair. Due to limited resources, the Trees & Sidewalks Program is only able to repair the most severely damaged sites across all five boroughs. We agree that additional funding would increase the capacity of this program, but additional funding cannot be accommodated with current staffing levels.

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: Install new street trees and replace dead or damaged trees in priority areas to maintain canopy coverage and improve environmental and aesthetic conditions. This ensures long-term community benefits while addressing gaps in the tree canopy.
rows.headline: Other capital budget request for DPR
rows.response: Agency supports and can accommodate Explanation: Through our new Neighborhood Tree Planting approach, we will be planting trees in every viable location across the city on a predictable 9-year cycle, prioritizing the most heat-vulnerable neighborhoods first. Find out when we will be planting each neighborhood on the Parks website: https://www.nycgovparks.org/trees/street-tree-planting. As part of this approach, we will also be removing dead trees and stumps and replacing them with new trees where feasible.
